tb21_profile.skill: Extract the date from each filename, build four inclusive windows (today, trailing 7, trailing 30, month-to-date) against a fixed reference date, tally three severity tokens per window, and emit an exactly-ordered CSV including zero rows
tb21_profile.domain: Shell/Python log processing: date parsing and calendar arithmetic, severity-level counting, strict CSV output contract
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec: a single-pass aggregation report whose whole difficulty is boundary conditions and output-schema fidelity

verifier_notes: No grade I disagreed with. Worth flagging that the two closest Terminal-Lego matches split: task_11217 is strong (12 tests, 6 pinned) while task_11201, essentially the same task, is only weak (1 pinned of 10); I ranked task_11217 first partly for that reason. The entire Recursive-Task-Synthesis slate is absent, as expected for that corpus -- rts_task_dbfe7fd6f98ef686d4971762 is a genuine skill match but ships no verifier in our copy, and I could not find a graded equivalent that counts INFO/WARNING/ERROR across a log directory as directly.

notes: This is the task where boilerplate overlap is worst: every corpus has hundreds of 'parse logs, write a CSV' tasks and the retrieval order is dominated by them. I filtered on the one thing that is actually hard here -- inclusive relative-date-window arithmetic anchored to a fixed 'today' -- and the winners change completely. Terminal-Lego-15k genuinely beats the old pool: task_11217 and task_11201 (decide file age from the date in the filename versus a relative cutoff) are the closest matches in the entire 76k pool and the v1 corpora have no equivalent. CalibForge also beats the old pool, with a YYYY-MM-DD-named-daily-files task and a DST-aware streak engine, both strongly verified. SWE-Smith is unexpectedly useful because the arrow date library is in it -- ten date-arithmetic bugs with repo-tests verification -- so judge it on skill/domain and ignore the task_form penalty. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has one real match (the severity index) and a cluster of six near-duplicate 'last 30 days of git history' tasks; I kept four of them, and the merge step should treat them as one item, not four.
